summary_paragraph: A man with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, type II diabetes, and chronic heart failure was admitted due to worsening gangrene and infection in his right fourth toe, which had not improved since a prior admission. Imaging revealed osteomyelitis and subcutaneous gas, prompting surgical intervention. He underwent multiple procedures, including amputation of the third, fourth, and fifth toes and a completion transmetatarsal amputation. Cultures from the surgical site grew methicillin-sensitive Staphylococcus aureus and Veillonella species, and he was treated with targeted IV antibiotics, later transitioned to oral Augmentin and metronidazole. His postoperative course was stable, though he experienced asymptomatic bradycardia, noted on telemetry, with cardiology recommending pacemaker evaluation if episodes recur. He participated in physical therapy, was deemed non-weight-bearing on the right lower extremity, and was discharged to a rehabilitation facility with wound care instructions and a follow-up appointment scheduled in two weeks.
